applicable_failures: The filename filter `relname` is restrictive: it allows only certain agreement names (purchase, merger, spa, jv, investment, etc.). Signed deals whose agreements use other names (e.g. 'definitive agreement', 'transaction agreement', 'contribution', 'stock sale') would be dropped silently. The script's own output shows only 141 hits, with no check against the broader file set.

The scan output is mostly unreviewed (+112629 chars truncated in the log). The agent self-assessed 'goal reached' and named matters from the hit list without opening any of them. Per the list, none of the 1001-00003 through 1046-00001 matters were opened. Hit status (signed vs draft) was inferred from file names such as 'execution'.
The 141 hits include hits the agent itself calls unrelated (securities/fund/loan/escrow). The agent therefore did not separate qualifying from non-qualifying hits in this stage.
critique.concerns: A single proximity scan with a restrictive filename filter produced 141 hits. The agent then claimed full coverage without checking that the filter did not drop differently named agreements. Signed vs negotiating status rests on filename guesses. The candidate list is mixed with noise and is large. Nothing was verified by opening documents. The run did finish, with no timeout, so the failure is the filter, not partial coverage.
critique.recommendation: Compare the scan's matter list against a broader scan that has no filename filter, using the fraud and cap/basket proximity regex on all .docx files. Add any newly surfaced matters to the candidates. Then open each candidate agreement to confirm it is signed, to check the fraud carve-out wording, and to confirm the deal type.

Common failures at this stage in past runs:
- An uncapped store-wide scan with broad or common terms printed snippets for every match, producing millions of characters that filled the context before any response was written.
- A store-wide scan timed out or printed nothing after reaching only part of the store, and the agent accepted the partial output instead of narrowing by matter range or folder, rerunning, or searching file names, so qualifying matters never entered the candidate set.
- A scan had already surfaced every needed matter, but a follow-up filter on file names, folder names, exact phrases, or a hand-picked list silently dropped matters whose documents were named or worded differently.
- Matters were listed in file-name searches or scan output, but later scripts restricted to certain names or folders so the needed matter was never opened or examined.
What successful runs did: Passing runs also hit timeouts, but their output stayed bounded enough to read, and they often split the scan into parallel matter-range scripts or narrowed to a key acronym or per-matter hit counts, then picked candidates from what was reached.
Reconsider before moving on. If the goal was not fully reached, or any failure above applies, reopen this stage now: call stage_start with stage="Scan document text with an extraction script" and a goal that says what you will fix. Otherwise call stage_start for the next stage you need.
